module: Mark synthetic outputs and verify detection

lesson.title: Upstream suppliers, downstream systems and dates
lesson.summary: Verify the downstream provider's own route and apply the targeted marking transition.

prerequisites.reason: The learner must distinguish operative law from interpretation and voluntary methods.
The learner must allocate the relevant duty before choosing an implementation.
The learner must distinguish machine marking from human-facing labels. The learner must connect each marker to its verification mechanism.
The learner must evaluate the four legal qualities before judging a method or supplier.

blocks: A **downstream system provider** integrates an upstream model or service into its own AI system. Upstream marking may support its compliance, but it remains responsible for the system it provides.

Ask what is marked, how detection works, whether Harbour preserves the markers and whether the actual delivery path is covered. Self-hosting does not automatically make an organisation a model provider; assess the actions and objects supplied.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 50(2), 111(4), 113; Guidelines paragraphs 71-74, 153-154
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation
Final Transparency Code, 10 June 2026; voluntary implementation framework

blocks: Procurement should seek implementation evidence, access to detection, limitations and responsibilities for correction. A supplier logo or Code signature is not a test report for Harbour's integration.

The Code addresses non-removal in a provider's own processing pipeline and reasonable value-chain cooperation. Verify transformations within Harbour's control rather than asserting it can police every later copy everywhere.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 50(2), 111(4), 113; Guidelines paragraphs 71-74, 153-154
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation
Final Transparency Code, 10 June 2026; voluntary implementation framework

blocks: **Application date** means when obligations apply, which differs from entry into force. Article 50's default application is 2 August 2026 under Article 113.

Article 111(4) gives providers of systems placed on the market or put into service **before 2 August 2026** until **2 December 2026** to comply with Article 50(2). It is a targeted marking/detection transition, not a postponement of every transparency duty.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 50(2), 111(4), 113; Guidelines paragraphs 71-74, 153-154
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation
Final Transparency Code, 10 June 2026; voluntary implementation framework

blocks: A qualifying older assistant may receive that paragraph 2 transition while still needing its applicable interaction disclosure from 2 August. A new system first placed on the market on 3 August does not qualify for the earlier-system transition.
Check the system's placement or service date, not just the date its model was trained or the supplier company was founded.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 50(2), 111(4), 113; Guidelines paragraphs 71-74, 153-154
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation
Final Transparency Code, 10 June 2026; voluntary implementation framework

blocks: Commission guidance separately addresses old outputs. It does not require retroactive marking/labelling of qualifying pre-2 August generated media; for public-interest text, both generation/manipulation and publication before that date matter.

Text generated in July but first published to inform the public after 2 August needs the later publication analysis. This is interpretation about content dates, distinct from Article 111(4)'s system transition. Use the later publication lessons for its precise disclosure conditions.

questions.prompt: Harbour wraps a supplier's marked generation service but its export removes the marker. May it rely solely on the supplier's claim?

options.blocks: No; verify and repair the actual downstream route
options.reason: Harbour's own product path must support its provider obligations.

options.blocks: Yes; the upstream company carries every later duty

options.reason: Hosting architecture is not a general exemption.

variants.prompt: Does upstream marking settle Harbour's provider duty when its integration strips that marking?

options.blocks: Yes; the upstream company carries every later duty

options.reason: Hosting architecture is not a general exemption.

options.blocks: No; verify and repair the actual downstream route

questions.prompt: An assistant was put into service on 1 July 2026. Which duty receives the Article 111(4) transition to 2 December?

options.reason: Interaction and other disclosure duties are not generally postponed by this rule.
The AI Act transition does not defer those separate laws.

variants.prompt: What is postponed by the targeted transition for a qualifying pre-2 August system?

options.reason: The AI Act transition does not defer those separate laws.
Interaction and other disclosure duties are not generally postponed by this rule.

questions.prompt: A provider first puts a generator into service on 3 August 2026. May it use the earlier-system transition solely because training occurred in July?

options.blocks: Yes; every new generator receives four extra months
options.reason: The transition is confined to qualifying existing systems.

options.blocks: No; the relevant earlier placement or service condition is unmet
options.reason: The rule concerns the system's placement/service, not its training date.

options.blocks: Yes; training date always controls the transition
